**Finding submitted: compliant** (confidence 0.90) — no redline proposed.

**Summary:** The AUDIT rule protects our party from burdensome audits. In this Transfer and Servicing Agreement, the direction of every audit-type right is reversed from the typical vendor-contract posture: our parties (Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A as Issuer and Verizon ABS LLC as Depositor) are the *beneficiaries* of the review rights, and Cellco (Servicer/Custodian/Marketing Agent) is the party subject to them.

Because there is no audit, inspection, verification or system-access right exercisable against the Issuer or Depositor anywhere in the document, there is no exposure to cap and the rule is satisfied at the preferred level. Consistent with the instruction not to flag obligations that benefit our party, I did not touch Section 3.6, Section 3.4(e), the Article XIV Asset Representations Review access provisions, or the Regulation AB reporting package — tightening any of those would erode our own oversight rights.

One drafting observation, recorded in the rationale rather than raised as a deviation: our Section 3.6 and 3.4(e) review rights are silent on who bears the cost of a review and are expressly subject to the Servicer's own confidentiality, privacy and data protection policies. That is a limitation on rights running *in our favour*, so it falls outside this rule — but it may be worth raising under a servicer-oversight or information-rights rule if one exists in the playbook.
